title: runtime: a hook or job body that fails to compile reports the generic `<kind> 'NAME' threw: SyntaxError …` sentence, not the coded compile-failure an action body gets (found on #34987)
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTggz8AL2bCABoDGis

Filed by the #34987 card thread at the seat's direction. Found by that card's dev (PR #35713, out-of-scope note in report 7028030483); not started, per the seat's p1-only rule.

## What happens
`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts` (at `main` c03a8a342, ~line 456) codes a compile failure only for actions:

```ts
if (args.origin.kind === 'action' && isCompileFailure(err)) {
  throw actionBodyCompileFailure(args.origin.name, formatErr(err));
}
throw new SandboxError(`${args.origin.kind} '${args.origin.name}' threw: ${formatErr(err)}`, …);
```

A hook or job body that does not compile in its wrapper `(async (ctx) => { SOURCE })` therefore surfaces at run time as the generic `hook 'NAME' threw: SyntaxError: …` (or `job 'NAME' threw: …`), the same sentence a body that ran and threw gets, instead of the coded compile-failure sentence an action body gets. PR #35713 adds the author-time refusal (`hook-body-does-not-compile`, `job-body-does-not-compile`), so this is reached only by a body that bypassed the authoring doors (stored before the rule, or loaded without lint).

## Reproduce
1. Register a hook whose `body.source` is `const ctx = 1; return;` (or a job with the same body), skipping `os validate`.
2. Trigger it. The runner's error reads `hook '<name>' threw: SyntaxError: Identifier 'ctx' has already been declared`.
3. Compare an action with `const input = 1; return;`: it answers the coded compile failure from `actionBodyCompileFailure`.

## Done when
A hook or job body that fails to compile reports a coded compile-failure sentence naming the hook or job and the compile error, distinguishable from a body that ran and threw, the way actions do; a pin covers one hook and one job.

Grade: left to triage.
